summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy was admitted for acute shortness of breath and hypertensive urgency. She presented with orthopnea and palpitations, and was found to have pulmonary edema and severely elevated blood pressure. She was treated in the ICU with nitroglycerin infusion, CPAP, and hemodialysis, which improved her respiratory status and blood pressure. Her heart rhythm remained stable, and no acute ischemia was detected. She was started on inhaled bronchodilators and a short course of antibiotics due to mild bronchospasm and leukocytosis, though no active infection was confirmed. Her medications were optimized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for pulmonary function testing and anticoagulation monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
